To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best predictors of aging are diffusion and iron deposition, and that these predictors are distributed across the brain in a non-homogeneous way, and that they are not correlated with macroscopic atrophy.
“We explored for the first age-related variation on four quantitative MR markers and found that iron deposition and microstructure damage are more sensitive to aging than macroscopic tissue atrophy”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the analysis of multimodal MRI data.
the development of a new method for the analysis of multimodal MRI data, based on a voxel-based approach.
the study of normal brain aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best predictor for each voxel in a given area is the one with the largest effect size (i.e. the one with the highest R-square value).
the best biomarker to predict age-induced structural change is not a unique one but depends on the specific brain area under investigation.
the best predictor of age-related structural brain changes depends on the brain region of interest and that the use of a multimodal approach is mandatory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) the method can be used for the identification of the best predictors of physiological aging in the brain, and that: 2) the best predictors are not the same for each brain region, and that 3) the best predictors for most brain regions are sensitive to iron deposition and tissue damage rather than to atrophy.

the voxel-based multiple regression of quantitative biomarkers can be used for the identification of the most sensitive predictors of age-related changes, for the identification of age-related changes that cannot be detected by conventional MRI, and for the characterization of the spatial distribution of different age-related pathologies.

(i) the combination of different MR biomarkers provides a better description of the aging brain, (ii) the combination of MR biomarkers and physiological variables allows to better understand the underlying mechanisms of brain aging and (iii) voxel-based regression of multiple MR biomarkers provides an unbiased and powerful approach to identify the best biomarker for the study of brain aging in a given voxel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a voxel-based multiple regression of multiple MR modalities is a powerful tool to identify the best predictor of age-related structural changes in the brain.
a voxel-based multiple regression approach allows to simultaneously identify in each voxel of the brain the best quantitative biomarker of age-related changes.
the voxel-based multiple regression approach is a promising method for the analysis of multimodal MRI data, allowing to identify in a voxel-wise manner the best predictor of a physiological process.
